title: Taking a Look at Star Wars: Outer Rim, with the Unfinished Business Expansion
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gy_rDsWx8_4

Daniel (@dungeondive) pauses a solo game of Star Wars: Outer Rim midway, playing the bounty hunter Bossk against an AI Lando Calrissian who is trouncing him, to explain why he finally bought a game he had circled for years. The Unfinished Business expansion is the reason. The base game had many decks but thin ones, often ten cards, and he believes sandbox games live or die on the feeling that anything can happen. The expansion adds cards to every deck, AI decks for bounty hunters as well as smugglers, a custom AI card per character, end caps that close the half-circle board into a ring, and a contact-reveal icon that finally makes bounty hunting viable. He thinks Fantasy Flight should simply bundle it.

He answers the questions he expects. Is it fun if you do not like Star Wars? He is the test case, sick of the franchise for twenty years, and he is having a blast, because the pick-up-and-deliver, bounty-hunting sandbox with quick turns stands on its own. How does it compare to Xia? Xia is crunchier and more open; this is more of a popcorn movie with better little story moments and a stronger solo mode. Firefly he skipped for its table footprint. The AI opponent is a glorified timer, but a thematic one that engages with the board rather than counting down. His complaints are the licence, the board shape, and the expansion being mandatory.

----

Daniel calls the AI opponent a "glorified timer" that works because it feels thematic. Which solo AI has convinced you it was a rival rather than a clock?
